description: Forecast a time series (sales, demand, traffic, costs…) with prediction intervals — and check it the way a forecaster would instead of trusting one model: Holt-Winters, automatic ARIMA/SARIMA and the two naive baselines (last value, same period last season) are all backtested with a rolling origin, and the answer says whether any model actually beats the naive baseline (often none does: then the honest forecast is the naive one), how much of the promised interval coverage was really achieved, anomalies, and a likely level shift. Daily series can take official holidays (Spain by region and other countries) or your own dates, and their effect is estimated. Deterministic; nothing leaves the machine.

arimaOrder.description: Fixed ARIMA orders; default: chosen automatically by AICc

data.description: The series as text: one value per line, or "date;value" per line (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM; separator ; , or tab; a header line is skipped). Alternative to values

dates.description: With values: one date per value (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM). Daily or monthly dates set the default season (7 or 12) and date the forecast

holidayCalendar.description: Official holidays to add: a country ("ES", "PT", "FR", "DE"…) or a Spanish region ("ES-MD", "ES-CT"…). Daily series only

holidays.description: Your own holiday dates (YYYY-MM-DD), past and future. Daily series only

horizon.description: Steps to forecast. Default: one season (or 12)

model.description: Model whose forecast is returned. auto = the lowest error on the backtest. All are always compared

season.description: Seasonal period: 7 for daily data with a weekly pattern, 12 for monthly, 1 for none. Default: from the dates, else 1

values.description: The series as numbers, oldest first. Alternative to data

name: forecast
title: Forecast a time series, with an honest backtest
